- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) — adjust downward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimate when sentiment is negative or near zero — increase forecast by 2–5% for the first 3–5 days to catch upward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes (e.g., >70) — cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >80 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.25 after 3–5 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid overfitting to recent 7-day highs — use 14-day rolling mean as baseline for adjustment.
